heading: Listener options: condition, Order and InBackground
body: A listener hears one model, the type of its parameter. It can also have a condition. A condition is a small, limited expression that uses value and event. Tachyon compiles it once into a matcher, and every runtime evaluates that matcher. Order(n) runs the listeners of one event from the lowest number up. Listeners with the same number run in the order you declare them. A listener without Order has the number 0. A listener publishes again when its return type is a model: the value it returns, or each of up to 32 values in a returned list, is published as that model. Tachyon ignores any other return value. InBackground makes a listener run later, after the current delivery pass. Such a detached listener never publishes again, as in Spring. In Tac, InBackground works in every language, because the page's event bus delays the delivery itself. In Yon, it needs a language with asynchronous methods: JavaScript, TypeScript and Python accept it. The other Yon languages reject it at compile time: PHP, Java, Groovy, Kotlin, C#, Rust, Dart, Go and Ruby. An id names a listener in diagnostics (error and warning messages).
